subject: ORD function
notes: Re-verified independently. The canonical PDF was re-extracted at PDF page 930 (printed folio 900): the general format is literally 'FUNCTION ORD ( argument-1 )' — no brackets, no optional element, so there is no room for the falsely-restrictive OCR failure mode; the §15.70.2 transcription is faithful. Grammar (read, not inferred): functionCall : FUNCTION functionName (LPAREN functionArgList? RPAREN)? ; ORD is not a reserved word and reaches functionName as an ordinary word. Exact arity 1 comes from the catalog row Add(new("ORD", IntrinsicType.Integer, IntrinsicArity.Fixed, 1, 1, "s", "Ord", IntrinsicBind.Runtime, false, 85)) and is enforced by BindIntrinsicCore's MinArgs/MaxArgs gate. RE-PROBED with the built CLI at --std 2023: 'FUNCTION ORD' and 'FUNCTION ORD()' each give COBOL1504 '1 argument(s); 0 given', 'FUNCTION ORD(A B)' gives '1 argument(s); 2 given', and the one-argument form binds. Both test-refs exist on disk and both call the one-argument format with value assertions (IF127A has 10 FUNCTION ORD call sites).
